steps.text: The simulation page displays its configuration form: pick a saved allocation key, name the simulation, set the injection, and upload the consumption file to simulate.
steps.title: Simulation page

steps.text: Open the "Allocation key" dropdown and select the key you just saved. The simulation will apply this allocation to the imported consumption data.
steps.title: Choose the allocation key

steps.text: Give the simulation a name so you can find it in the history.
steps.title: Name the simulation

steps.text: Enter the name of the column in your data file that holds the energy produced.
steps.title: Injection name

steps.text: Upload the same "test_4.csv" file into the drop zone. The simulation will compute self-consumption and energy sharing from this data and the selected key.
steps.title: Import the file to simulate

steps.text: Click "Run simulation". The simulation is queued and appears in the runs list with a "Pending" status until the computation completes.
steps.title: Launch the simulation

steps.text: The computation takes a moment: refresh the list to see its result.
steps.title: Refresh

steps.text: Click the finished simulation to show its results.
steps.title: Expand the simulation

steps.text: The simulation is complete. The headline metrics are shown: self-consumed energy, surplus, self-sufficiency rate, and sharing rate — computed from the saved key and the imported file.
steps.title: Simulation results

steps.text: Expand an iteration to see how the energy was shared in it.
steps.title: Per-iteration detail

steps.text: Each key iteration can be expanded to reveal the per-consumer detail: allocation, consumption, self-consumed energy, surplus, and residual volume. This is where allocation solutions are compared.
steps.title: Per-iteration, per-consumer detail
